title: MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I DEFICIENCY, NUCLEAR TYPE 7

relationships.phenotype: MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I DEFICIENCY, NUCLEAR TYPE 7

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NDUFV2 gene (600532) on chromosome 18p11.

checks.claim: Mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NDUFV2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The homozygous mutation altering the consensus splice-donor site of exon 2 resulted in 70% decreased NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.
checks.explanation: Homozygous NDUFV2 mutation causes complex I deficiency; MC1DN7 is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The NDUFV2 gene is located on chromosome 18p11.
checks.evidence_quote: a 4-bp deletion in intron 2 (IVS2+5_+8delGTAA) of the NDUFV2 gene (encoding NADH dehydrogenase ubiquinone flavoprotein 2)
checks.explanation: The paper does not give the location. The claim is treated as supported because it is standard nomenclature for the gene.

paragraphs.text: Mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is a disorder of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I. Bénit et al. (2003) described early-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with trunk hypotonia and encephalopathy in affected individuals. Cameron et al. (2015) reported a high lactate/pyruvate ratio in fibroblasts. Respiratory chain complex I deficiencies are a genetically heterogeneous group of diseases resulting from mutations in either mitochondrial or nuclear DNA (Bénit et al., 2003).

paragraphs.text: Respiratory chain complex I deficiencies are a genetically heterogeneous group of diseases, and mutations in a number of genes encoding complex I subunits have been reported (Bénit et al., 2003). Loeffen et al. (2001) noted that attention had mainly focused on the relation between complex I deficiency and mtDNA mutations.

paragraphs.text: Using a combination of denaturing high performance liquid chromatography and sequence analysis, Bénit et al. (2003) identified a homozygous 4-bp deletion in intron 2 of the NDUFV2 gene (IVS2+5_+8delGTAA) in 3 affected sibs of a consanguineous family with complex I deficiency. The mutation altered the consensus splice donor site.
